---
title: "Asynchronous Background Processing"
format: html
---

In native desktop applications, responsiveness is paramount. If a user triggers a 10-second data processing job or model fitting calculation on the main thread, the window freezes, controls become unresponsive, and the OS may flag the app as "Not Responding".

RDesk includes a built-in asynchronous worker engine that moves heavy execution to background processes while streaming progress and results back to the interface.

## Quick Example: `async()` Helper

Wrapping your handler callback in `async()` executes it in a background process automatically:

```r
# R/server.R
app$on_message("run_simulation", async(function(payload) {
  # This code runs in a background process!
  n <- payload$iterations
  Sys.sleep(2) # Simulating heavy computation
  result <- mean(rnorm(n))
  
  list(mean = result, n = n)
}, app = app, loading_message = "Running simulation..."))
```

When the handler is invoked:

1. RDesk sends a loading state event (`__loading__`) to the frontend displaying `"Running simulation..."`.
2. The task runs in a background process without blocking the main event loop.
3. Once completed, the result is sent back to the frontend, and the loading state automatically clears.

## Progress Reporting with `async_progress()`

For multi-step operations (e.g. processing files or training epochs), you can push live progress bars to the user interface:

```r
app$on_message("process_batches", async_progress(function(payload, update_progress) {
  total_batches <- 10
  
  for (i in seq_len(total_batches)) {
    Sys.sleep(0.5) # Process batch
    
    pct <- round((i / total_batches) * 100)
    update_progress(
      percent = pct, 
      message = sprintf("Processing batch %d of %d...", i, total_batches)
    )
  }
  
  list(status = "complete", batches = total_batches)
}, app = app))
```

### Listening in JavaScript

On the frontend, listen for the `progress` event:

```javascript
rdesk.on("progress", function(state) {
  var progressBar = document.getElementById("my-progress-bar");
  var statusText = document.getElementById("status-text");
  
  progressBar.style.width = state.percent + "%";
  statusText.textContent = state.message;
});
```

## Backend Options: `callr` vs. `mirai`

RDesk supports two async execution backends:

```r
# Force callr backend (recommended for standalone Windows bundles)
options(rdesk.async_backend = "callr")

# Use mirai daemon worker pool (high-throughput, zero process spawn overhead)
options(rdesk.async_backend = "mirai")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Recommended Backend in Standalone Bundles
In standalone Windows distributions, **`callr`** is the recommended default backend because it uses standard OS process pipes rather than local domain sockets, avoiding firewall and antivirus socket inspection on locked-down client machines.
:::

## Job Management & Cancellation

You can manage active background jobs programmatically:

```r
# List currently running jobs
active_jobs <- rdesk_jobs_list()

# Check pending job count
count <- rdesk_jobs_pending()

# Cancel an active job by ID
rdesk_cancel_job(job_id = "job_123")
```
